title: Service Container aur Dependency Injection
objectives: `bind`, `singleton` aur contextual binding ka farak jaanna
Container ko testing mein swap karna

sections.heading: Dependency Injection kya hai?
sections.body:
Agar class ko kisi aur class ki zarurat hai (dependency), to woh use khud `new` se nahi banati, balki bahar se **inject** hoti hai. Isse code loosely coupled aur testable rehta hai.

**Service container** Laravel ka woh tool hai jo classes banata hai aur unki dependencies khud dhundh kar inject karta hai.

sections.heading: Real-world example: Payment gateway
sections.body: Checkout ko payment gateway chahiye. Aaj Razorpay hai, kal doosra ho sakta hai. Agar `new RazorpayGateway()` controller mein likh diya to badalna mushkil hoga. Interface + container se ek jagah badalna kaafi hai.

code.code:
<?php

namespace App\Contracts;

interface PaymentGateway
{
    public function charge(int $amount): bool;
}

<?php

namespace App\Services;

use App\Contracts\PaymentGateway;

class RazorpayGateway implements PaymentGateway
{
    public function charge(int $amount): bool
    {
        return $amount > 0; // asli API call yahan aayegi
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Contracts\PaymentGateway;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class CheckoutController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(private PaymentGateway $gateway) {}

    public function pay(Request $request)
    {
        $paid = $this->gateway->charge(500);

        return $paid ? 'Payment ho gaya' : 'Payment fail';
    }
}

explain: Controller sirf `PaymentGateway` interface jaanta hai, concrete class nahi.
Laravel controller banate waqt constructor ke type-hint dekhta hai aur object inject karta hai.

sections.heading: Auto-resolution aur binding
sections.body: Agar type-hint ek normal class hai (jiski dependencies bhi resolve ho sakti hain), to container bina setup ke object bana deta hai. **Interface** ke liye batana padta hai ki kaunsi class use karni hai. Yeh **binding** service provider ke `register` mein karte hain.

code.code:
<?php

namespace App\Providers;

use App\Contracts\PaymentGateway;
use App\Services\RazorpayGateway;
use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;

class AppServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        $this->app->bind(PaymentGateway::class, RazorpayGateway::class);
    }

    public function boot(): void
    {
        //
    }
}

explain: `bind()` – jab bhi `PaymentGateway` maango, `RazorpayGateway` ka naya object do.
Is binding ke baad controller mein kuch badalna nahi padta.

sections.heading: singleton, contextual binding aur manual resolve
sections.body: Alag zarurat ke liye alag tareeke:
explain: `bind` har baar naya object, `singleton` ek hi object baar-baar.
Contextual binding mein alag classes ko alag implementation de sakte ho.
`app(Foo::class)` helper se kahin bhi object mil jaata hai, par normally constructor injection behtar hai.

sections.heading: Testing mein swap
sections.body: Test mein asli payment nahi chahiye. Container mein fake object daal do:

callout.text: Yehi DI ka sabse bada fayda hai: asli cheez ki jagah fake dena bahut aasaan ho jaata hai.

versionDiff.heading: Container: Laravel 11, 12, 13
versionDiff.intro: Service container ka behaviour teeno versions mein same hai. Farak sirf yeh hai ki bindings kahan likhte hain.

items.11: Bindings `app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php` ke `register()` mein. Naye providers `bootstrap/providers.php` mein listed hote hain.
items.13: Same. PHP 8.3+ guaranteed hai, to `#[\Override]` jaise features use kar sakte ho.

errors.error: Target [App\Contracts\PaymentGateway] is not instantiable while building [App\Http\Controllers\CheckoutController]
errors.cause: Interface ki binding nahi hai, container ko pata nahi kaunsi class deni hai.
errors.fix: Service provider ke `register()` mein `$this->app->bind(Interface::class, Concrete::class)` jodo.

errors.error: Unresolvable dependency resolving [Parameter #0 [ <required> string $apiKey ]] in class ...
errors.cause: Constructor mein simple type (string/int) hai jiski value container ko nahi pata.
errors.fix: Binding closure mein value do, ya `->needs('$apiKey')->give(config('services.x.key'))` use karo.

errors.error: Binding badli par purana object chal raha hai
errors.cause: Cache ya provider ka cached data.

debug.body: Container se kya resolve ho raha hai Tinker mein turant dekh sakte ho.

quiz.why: Class ki zarurat ki cheezein bahar se (constructor/method) di jaati hain.

quiz.q: Interface ko concrete class se kahan bind karte hain?
quiz.why: Bindings service provider ke `register()` method mein hote hain.

options: `singleton` ek hi object share karta hai, `bind` har baar naya
quiz.why: Singleton ek baar banta hai aur reuse hota hai.

interview.a: Laravel ka dependency management tool jo classes ko resolve karta hai aur unki dependencies inject karta hai.

interview.q: Constructor injection aur method injection mein farak?
interview.a: Constructor injection class ki dependencies object ke liye set karta hai. Method injection sirf us method ke liye dependency deta hai, jaise controller method mein `Request $request`.
Taaki code concrete class par depend na kare aur implementation badalna ya fake dena aasan ho.
`bind` har resolve par naya instance, `singleton` ek shared instance.

interview.q: Container testing mein kaise madad karta hai?
interview.a: `$this->app->instance()` ya `bind()` se asli service ki jagah fake/mock inject kar sakte ho.

summary: DI mein dependencies bahar se aati hain.
Service container objects banata aur inject karta hai.
Normal classes auto-resolve hoti hain, interfaces ko binding chahiye.
`bind` har baar naya, `singleton` ek hi object.
Testing mein `instance()` se fake inject karo.
